key_insight: PiPS adds prototype-based explanations to semantic segmentation after training, so a pre-trained model can explain its pixel-level predictions without being modified.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging workflows, this could help clinicians inspect why a segmentation model marked specific anatomical regions while keeping the original model’s performance unchanged.
method: Extracts post-hoc prototypical explanations from any pre-trained segmentation network
Produces spatially localized, human-interpretable visual similarities for dense predictions
Requires no retraining, fine-tuning, or architectural changes
evidence_signal: The abstract claims the approach works on any pre-trained model and preserves 100% of the original predictive performance, but it does not report dataset size or quantitative benchmark results here.
watch_item: Because the explanation is generated after the fact, its clinical usefulness will still depend on how faithfully the prototypes reflect the model’s true decision process in real cases.
paper_title: PiPS: Post-Hoc Prototypical Explanations for Interpretable Semantic Segmentation
